Help Curveon identify your bike\'s fuel signal and calibrate the gauge

Bikes report fuel levels differently, so Curveon can\'t always detect it automatically. Tap a button before and after filling up — Curveon uses the litres from the pump to identify the right signal. After two fill-ups, the gauge shows litres. Your readings are saved between rides.

Park on level ground the same way every time (always side stand or always centre stand), with the ignition on, engine off, and the OBD2 adapter plugged in. Keep the engine off so the fuel float stays steady — and for safety at the pump. Tap the circle when ready.
Enter your bike\'s full tank capacity in litres (check the owner\'s manual).

Park at the pump and tap Before filling. Fill until the nozzle clicks off, park the same way, and enter the litres shown on the pump. Do this twice, ideally with different amounts, without riding in between.
Entered the wrong amount? Tap × to remove it and try again. The active signal will be cleared if the remaining data isn\'t enough.

Fuel sensors are rarely linear. Adding extra readings between empty and full makes the litre display more accurate — for example after pouring a known amount from a can. Always park the same way with the engine off.
Pick the reading in step 4 first.
Not sure how much is left? Don\'t register it. Never run the bike dry on purpose.

Maps, curvy routes, music and messages on one screen — built for motorcycles and works offline. Here\'s a quick look at what Curveon can do.
Search for towns, addresses, fuel or cafés — even offline. You\'ll also find favourites, saved routes and roundtrips here, or press and hold on the map to start a trip.
All your trips in one place: imported GPX tracks, rides recorded automatically, planned trips and routes shared with friends.
Call favourites, recent callers and contacts with gloves on. Riding with a tablet on the bars? Curveon Companion on your phone forwards calls, messages and music over Bluetooth.
Download offline maps by country, link your phone, pick your language and customise maps and alerts. You can always replay this tour under Help.
Switch between a clean full-screen map and the dashboard with music and messages. A badge shows if you have unread messages.
Press and hold anywhere on the map to ride there, start a route, add a stop, save a favourite or check the speed limit and road surface.
See incoming messages and reply by voice through your headset — or swipe them away. Swipe the music card to switch between music apps.
With a Bluetooth OBD2 adapter on your bike, Curveon displays RPM, coolant temp, battery and fuel right beside the map.
You can always replay this tour and view every icon under Settings → Help.
